title: Implement latent-span-deferral and route-aware burst throttling to cut tracer hot-path costs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: High-throughput services are experiencing increased CPU and allocation pressure from the tracer hot path. Even when only a small fraction of requests are sampled, we still pay cost for span allocation, header copies, and encoding decisions per request. This is visible as a recurring latency tail and elevated p50 CPU across several prod services (see dashboards).

Goal: Reduce tracer CPU and allocation overhead on the hot path by deferring full span materialization until the sampling decision or an explicit trace request. Combine deferral with a lightweight route-aware burst throttle so that sampling commit work is gated under high QPS bursts. Maintain or improve tail detection fidelity and preserve downstream compatibility (OTLP/Zipkin/Datadog exports).

Success metrics: end-to-end tracer CPU reduced by >=30% on p50 across instrumented services under realistic workloads; total allocated bytes per request reduced by >=40%; tail detection recall for >99th percentile latency maintained within 5% of current baseline; no increase in error rates or request latency outside noise.
design_notes:
Approach: 1) Introduce a LatentSpan token (fixed 32B footprint) that is created synchronously in the hot path. It holds only: span-id, parent-id (if present), timestamp, and a small flags bitfield. 2) Defer allocation of full span struct and attribute copying until either: a) the sampling controller returns 'commit' (probabilistic or reservoir decision), b) a tail-detector (local heuristics + kernel hints) marks the request as a candidate, or c) an explicit instrumentation API requests the full span. 3) Implement a route-aware burst token-bucket that limits sample-commits per route per second; excess latent spans are fast-path dropped or tagged minimal. 4) Add a lightweight local tail-detector using percentile counters + optional eBPF syscall/latency hints (enabled via runtime flag) to promote latent spans when a latency spike is detected. 5) On commit, allocate a pooled span object and populate attributes lazily using zero-copy views where possible. 6) Emit compressed/summary telemetry for deferred spans so console rollups and troubleshooting links remain useful.

Trade-offs considered: - Full deferral may lose some early attributes unless we snapshot small critical fields; we snapshot headers and request path lazily via reference-counted views. - eBPF hints improve tail recall but require elevated privileges; make this optional per deployment (Private/Dedicated vs Hosted). - Route-aware throttles risk under-sampling low-volume but high-SLO routes; we add per-route minimum budgets and a fast-path fallback to always sample 1/100k to keep observability on cold routes.

Implementation notes: use existing span-pool from runtime-1.20, extend with zero-copy header slice type. Keep hot-path in assembler-friendly code paths; avoid interface calls. Add metrics: latent_spans_created, latent_spans_committed, latent_spans_promoted, latent_spans_dropped_by_throttle, latent_span_alloc_bytes_saved.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Bench: end-to-end synthetic load (100k rps, mixed routes) shows >=30% reduction in tracer CPU p50 and >=40% allocation reduction per request. 2) Staging: rollout to canary hosts for 48h with no SLO regressions; trace recall for >99th percentile within 5% of baseline. 3) Feature flags: latent-span-deferral and kernel-hints must be behind flags. 4) Observability: new metrics visible in Console and dashboards; runbook updated. 5) Security: eBPF usage gated to Private/Dedicated; opt-in documented. 6) Documentation: SDK breaking changes documented and backward compatibility tests added.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature-flag prototype in a branch; unit tests + microbenchmarks. Phase 1: Canary rollout (5%) on low-risk services with latent-span-deferral enabled, kernel-hints disabled. Phase 2: Increase to 25% and enable route-aware throttle with conservative budgets. Phase 3: Enable kernel-hints on Dedicated staging only, compare recall. Phase 4: Full rollout across services with monitoring alarms and automated rollback if tail recall drops >7% or if request latency regresses. Post-mortem checklist and runbook updates before wider rollout.
comments: 2026-02-19 — Aisha Patel: Scoped initial design. Ran microbench to validate small latent token vs full span: observed ~38% allocation reduction on microbench when delaying attribute copy (baseline: runtime-1.20 tracer). Recording results to Confluence.

2026-02-25 — Marco Reyes: Prototype implemented: latent token path added behind feature flag. Initial perf test: p50 CPU reduced by 27% on service A; tail recall unchanged on 95th but down 3% at 99.9th — investigating promotion heuristics.

2026-03-02 — Eng Review: Discussed eBPF optionality. Security wants eBPF disabled by default for Hosted; allow opt-in for Dedicated/Private with documented risks. Action: add gating and runtime opt-in API.
2026-03-05 — QA: Added unit tests for pooled allocation; found a race when promoting latent spans with concurrent cancellation. Patch created in branch 'latent-span-fix-rc1'.

2026-03-10 — Marco Reyes: Bench run on mixed workload (90% simple, 10% heavy) shows allocation reduction 44% and overall tracer CPU reduction 33%. Created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2147

2026-03-12 — Observability: Dashboard created: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/latent-span-rollout (shows latent_spans_{created,committed,dropped} and route budgets). Linked to PR and canary logs.
2026-03-13 — Security: Confirmed kernel-hints require host-level capability; added deployment note for Private customers.
